subject: Media Arts
_width_axis_note: Width in media arts varies by the range of media forms, genres, platforms, technical tools and representational challenges students engage with. A student at minimum width works within one familiar media form or genre; wider students work across multiple forms, genres and increasingly complex representational problems.

AC9AMA8C01.minimum_width: Design a media arts work using at least one pre-production planning tool (storyboard, shooting script or production schedule); explain how the design choices communicate intended ideas, perspectives or meaning for an intended audience.
AC9AMA8C01.typical_width: Design and structure a media arts work using appropriate pre-production templates; make deliberate decisions about media languages, technical and symbolic elements; explain how design choices construct intended representations for a specific audience.
wider: Design a hybrid production that combines established genre conventions — trial multiple genre combinations and evaluate which best serves the intended meaning and audience
Experiment with technical and symbolic elements (sound, lighting, framing) to construct representations that deliberately challenge stereotyping, bias or unequal power relationships
Explore how to create representations that address issues such as identity, sustainable living or social justice — evaluate how media language choices construct the intended perspective
elaborations: using pre-production templates such as storyboard, shooting script or production schedule to plan production
understanding the importance of respectful relationships and empathy when developing characters to convey historical or cultural ideas
exploring ways to use media languages and technologies to create representations that perpetuate or challenge relationships or address issues such as stereotyping, bias, identity
experimenting with technical capabilities of media technologies and using media languages to inform plans for construction of representations
experimenting with technical and symbolic elements such as sound and lighting to construct representations for various genres or media platforms
experimenting with audio effects to construct ambient sound for different places or create/enhance atmosphere
experimenting with technical and symbolic elements to construct safe, legal, ethical and responsible representations
trialling ways to combine established genre conventions to make a hybrid production

AC9AMA8C02.minimum_width: Produce a media arts work using pre-production, production and post-production processes; explain how media arts concepts and responsible media practice are applied in the work.
AC9AMA8C02.typical_width: Apply production processes across pre-production, production and post-production to produce a media arts work for a specific audience; use media languages to construct representations; apply responsible media practice throughout.
wider: Produce a work that uses Viewpoints questions to interrogate own representational choices — 'What elements define the genre?', 'How can I create mood through images/sound/framing?' — document how questioning shapes production decisions
Combine established genre conventions across media types — transfer technical codes (framing, sound, typography) between media forms and evaluate how the transfer changes meaning
Produce a media arts work that creates a news story or social issue campaign — use media languages to construct perspective deliberately and evaluate how bias is constructed and can be challenged
elaborations: using pre-production, production and post-production processes to produce a media arts work representing sustainable futures or social justice
combining established genre conventions such as framing in still and moving images, sounds in radio/podcasts, font in print
transferring established technical codes between media types
using Viewpoints to ask questions about forms, elements, genre, mood and setting
producing a media arts work about sustainable habits or social justice
creating a news story focusing on an event to communicate perspective, using Viewpoints to consider bias

AC9AMA8D01.minimum_width: Develop at least one media production skill (e.g. camera operation, sound recording, editing) through deliberate practice; explain what improved and how it affects the work's ability to communicate.
AC9AMA8D01.typical_width: Develop media production skills across the production process; experiment with digital tools (cameras, sound equipment, editing/animation software) to construct representations; document skill development and its effect on representational quality.
wider: Experiment with digital tools including cameras, sound recording, editing/coding/animation software — evaluate how mastery of each tool expands representational possibilities
Construct fictional versions of everyday spaces using AR/VR or green screen — evaluate how these technologies create representations impossible in conventional media
Experiment with audio effects (sound effects, music, Foley sounds) to construct ambient sound — evaluate how audio construction changes the representational meaning of a scene
elaborations: exploring ways to use media languages and technologies to create representations that address issues of stereotyping, bias, identity, sustainable living
experimenting with technical capabilities and media languages to inform plans for design and construction of representations
experimenting with digital tools such as cameras, sound recording equipment or editing/coding/animation software
constructing fictional versions of everyday spaces using AR and VR
experimenting with audio effects to construct ambient sound
experimenting with story principles such as establishing setting/location or disrupting narrative structure
combining established genre conventions to make a hybrid production

AC9AMA8D02.minimum_width: Reflect on at least one creative choice in own media arts work and explain how it constructs a representation for an audience; document at least one refinement based on the reflection.
AC9AMA8D02.typical_width: Document and explain creative choices in relation to representations, genre codes and conventions; use Viewpoints questions to interrogate production decisions; reflect on potential audience engagement and refine accordingly.
wider: Use Viewpoints questions to interrogate own representational choices — 'How can I represent a range of views on this issue?', 'What do I need to change to create a stronger audience connection?' — document how questioning drives refinement

Explore media conventions and representations from another cultural context (e.g. cartooning genres in Asia) — use the investigation to inform own practice and develop understanding of cultural appropriation
Justify decisions made in the construction of representations by producers — evaluate how technical and symbolic codes are used to construct meaning and who benefits from those constructions
elaborations: observing and considering potential audience engagement to inform refinements across production processes
using Viewpoints to develop investigating questions about representing themes, concepts or ideas
documenting and explaining creative choices in relation to representations, genre codes and conventions
justifying decisions made by producers in construction of representations through technical and symbolic codes
using a storyboarding or editing template to annotate creative thinking when refining production
using Viewpoints for reflective questions about representing views and creating audience connection
exploring styles and representations from other cultural contexts to inform practice and understand cultural appropriation

AC9AMA8E01.minimum_width: Investigate how at least one media arts concept (e.g. cinematography, editing, sound, mise-en-scène) is used in a media work to construct representations; explain how the concept choices communicate meaning.
AC9AMA8E01.typical_width: Investigate how media arts concepts are used across cultures, times or contexts; analyse how technical and symbolic codes construct representations of people, places and events; explain how audiences are positioned to respond.
wider: Analyse how media languages are used to construct stereotypical representations in media products aimed at teenagers — evaluate how technical and symbolic codes produce and naturalise stereotypes
Investigate the ideology or philosophical viewpoint of a media work — analyse what institutions were involved in distribution and what the potential impact on audiences might be

Analyse how audiences are positioned to respond to different representations — investigate how depictions of cultural or social groups in Australian film and television construct meaning for diverse audiences
elaborations: identifying, describing and analysing how cinematography, mise-en-scène, editing or sound are manipulated to construct representations
using questions to analyse ideology and philosophical viewpoint of media works including institutional involvement and audience impact
analysing how media languages construct representations in media genres — how technical and symbolic codes produce stereotypical representations
analysing how audiences are positioned to respond to different representations through technical and symbolic codes

AC9AMA8E02.minimum_width: Explain what ICIP rights mean in a media arts context; give one example of what culturally responsive engagement with First Nations media arts looks like in practice.
AC9AMA8E02.typical_width: Investigate the diversity of First Nations Australian media arts works and practices with attention to ICIP rights; analyse choices First Nations media artists make about representations, story principles and audience relationships; apply ICIP understanding to own practice.
wider: Investigate a specific case of cultural appropriation in media arts where ICIP rights were denied — explain what happened, who was harmed, and what a respectful alternative would have looked like
Collaboratively construct guidelines for safe, ethical, legal and responsible media use — develop criteria for deciding whether ideas from existing cultural expressions can be used in new work
Investigate First Nations Australian media artists' choices about technical and symbolic elements, story principles and audience relationships — analyse how ICIP principles shape these choices
elaborations: exploring how knowledge of ICIP protocols helps students make ethical choices about content use
investigating cultural appropriation examples where ICIP rights have been denied in media arts
investigating choices First Nations Australian media artists make about technical elements, story principles, representations and audience relationships
collaboratively constructing guidelines to promote safe, ethical, legal and responsible media use
recognising how to select and use historical materials that accurately communicate First Nations perspectives
investigating issues relating to use of First Nations languages or stories in screen-based works

AC9AMA8P01.minimum_width: Present a media arts work to a specific audience using responsible media practices; reflect on the relationship the work created with the audience.
AC9AMA8P01.typical_width: Present media arts works considering potential audience relationships; apply copyright and ICIP responsibilities; evaluate how different presentation contexts affect audience interpretation and engagement.
wider: Distribute a media arts work using appropriate rights and permissions to an online space — evaluate how the distribution context shapes audience engagement
Present media arts works in different contexts (online platform, school exhibition) and evaluate how each context changes audience interpretation and response
Reflect on how relationships develop between media makers and audiences when planning presentation — evaluate how presentation choices create or limit audience connection
elaborations: distributing a media arts work designed to engage a specific audience using appropriate rights and permissions
complying with copyright laws and respecting ICIP rights when presenting media arts works
reflecting on how relationships develop between media arts makers and audiences
considering the impact of different audiences on interpretation and engagement
